Brod is retiring as Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer, stepping down from the latter role on July 31, 2020. Alice L. Jolla will become the new Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer effective July 31, 2020.

Bitcoin fell below US$8,000 for the first time since November amid regulatory threats, a US$500 million heist at Japan's Coincheck, and Facebook's ban on cryptocurrency ads. The price dropped as much as 16 percent before recovering to US$8,715, while other cryptocurrencies also tumbled.

President Trump criticized ABC for not apologizing to him following the cancellation of the Roseanne reboot over Roseanne Barr's racist tweet about Valerie Jarrett. While Trump claimed CEO Bob Iger did not call him, Jarrett stated Iger called her to apologize and express zero tolerance for the comments before canceling the show. Some Democratic lawmakers criticized Trump's response.

Nigerian firm Best Hope Services will launch the country's first online trade exhibition on May 1 to promote local innovations. The e-fair aims to allow exhibitors to showcase products globally and enable remote participation across sectors like technology and automobiles.

Microsoft is reportedly developing "Polaris," a modular version of Windows 10 built on Windows Core OS. Designed for desktops, laptops, and 2-in-1 devices, it will utilize the CShell interface and rely on UWP apps rather than legacy desktop applications to improve speed, security, and battery life. Microsoft may use remote virtualization to run legacy apps.

The Reagan-Bush Administration would follow five principles regarding China and the Far East, including maintaining a strategic partnership, promoting regional stability, and opposing aggression. Regarding Taiwan, the administration will follow the Taiwan Relations Act, which mandates maintaining peaceful relations and providing defensive weapons to protect Taiwan's security.

Researchers have determined how polypropylene's molecular regularity (isotacticity) and thermal treatment affect its mechanical properties. By understanding the relationship between isotacticity, crystallinity, and the elastic modulus, it is possible to synthesize materials with predetermined hardness or elasticity.

The JACL Kakehashi Program, supported by the Japan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, will select up to 200 Japanese or Asian American participants aged 18-25 for nine-day trips to Japan. Eligible applicants include college students or young professionals with bachelor's degrees. The program aims to build relations through cultural, political, and economic experiences.

Wal-Mart Stores Inc is bidding for clothing retailer Bonobos as part of an effort to compete with Amazon and reach younger customers. This potential acquisition follows previous purchases of online brands like ShoeBuy, Moosejaw, and ModCloth. While Wal-Mart is a major brick-and-mortar retailer, its online sales account for only about 3 percent of total sales.

Materials modeling of disordered materials faces challenges in obtaining atomistic structures that match experimental data. While Monte Carlo and hybrid reverse Monte Carlo methods exist, they often suffer from computational inefficiency or unphysical artifacts. This article introduces molecular augmented dynamics (MAD), an $O(N)$ modified molecular dynamics method designed to find low-energy, ab-initio accurate structures that match experimental data. MAD utilizes a Hamiltonian combining interatomic and experimental potentials to optimize both experimental agreement and system energy. The method provides analytical, linearly scaling forces for XRD, ND, PDF, and XPS observables while accounting for thermal broadening.

Intel has released Coffee Lake-based 14nm desktop processors and Z370 chipsets, with more processors and H310/B360 chipsets arriving in Q1 2018. Gemini Lake processors launch in November 2017. Notebook processors and enterprise vPro counterparts are planned for 2018, while 10nm Cannon Lake processors are expected in mid-2018, followed by Ice Lake in 2019.

Tips of the Week features various maker recommendations: Kent Barnes added rare earth magnets to tester wires for easier hookups; John Park converted an old AC motor into a rotating display turntable; Phillip Stokes suggested adding a hobby knife to a compass; Andy Birkey recommended marking untrue material edges with squiggly lines; an Instructable explains turning a drill press into a drum sander; and Ben Krasnow recommends an Ikea flexi-neck LED lamp for workbench lighting.

In 1976, Kent Howerton won the AMA 500cc National Motocross Championship opener in Mexico, New York, followed by Bob Hannah and Tony DiStefano. In 1982, Ricky Johnson won the High Point 250 National, while Darrell Shultz won the 500 Class. Additionally, Ross Pederson won the 1987 Montreal Supercross.

The "Drive & Kick" offense is a three-player weave initiated from a 3-2 spread alignment via dribble penetration. If the defense denies the drive, the handler passes back outside and replaces the receiver to continue the continuity. Options include kicking to a corner player if defenders zone or using a back cut if a defender sags.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, provides significant performance improvements for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads compared to the previous V100 generation. Key architectural features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types like TF32, BF16, and FP64, as well as fine-grained structured sparsity that can double throughput. The A100 introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, allowing a single GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU instances to improve utilization and provide quality of service. Additional enhancements include a larger L2 cache, high-bandwidth HBM2 memory, third-generation NVLink, and CUDA 11 advances such as asynchronous copy and task graph acceleration. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs to provide a scalable platform for large-scale AI infrastructure.

The Housing Authority of the City of Santa Barbara received a Gold Nugget Award for Bradley Studios, a 54-unit affordable development built in 2012. Designed by Peikert Group Architects LLP and built by McGillivray Construction, the project serves low and extremely low-income residents with special needs. The site includes community rooms and social service offices for mental health, addiction, and job training.

Using spatial transcriptomics and single-cell analysis, researchers identified immunosuppressive niches in cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) lesions characterized by the expression of immune checkpoints IDO1 and CD274 (PD-L1). These niches are primarily composed of myeloid cells, including mature dendritic cells and CCL18+ macrophages, which interact closely with IL-32-expressing CD8+ memory T cells and regulatory T cells (Tregs). A core gene signature associated with these niches across different forms of dermal leishmaniasis includes IL32, LYZ, GBP1, IFI30, and FTH1. In Sri Lankan CL patients, high abundance of IL-32+ CD8+ T cells is associated with slower treatment response, identifying IL-32 as a potential prognostic biomarker.

Acting CDC director Jim O’Neill called for the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine to be replaced with three separate monovalent shots. Experts state there is no evidence that separating the vaccine improves safety or effectiveness, and they note that monovalent versions are no longer available in the U.S.

The MSPM0C1105/6 are ultra-low-power 32-bit microcontrollers based on the Arm Cortex-M0+ core, operating at up to 32MHz with supply voltages from 1.62V to 3.6V. These devices include up to 64KB of embedded flash, 8KB of SRAM, a 3-channel DMA, and various analog and digital peripherals, including a 12-bit ADC, multiple timers, and communication interfaces such as UART, SPI, and I2C. The MCUs feature five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN) and utilize two power domains to balance performance and energy consumption.

This study explored the empathic profiles of 206 university teachers at the University of G in Spain using the Interpersonal Reactivity Index. Results indicated a high overall level of empathy, with optimal scores in perspective taking, fantasy, and empathic concern, and moderate scores in personal distress. Female participants scored significantly higher across all dimensions. No significant differences in empathy were found regarding degree program, campus, contractual status, or teaching experience, though prior non-university teaching experience related to specific dimensions.

The Department advises against dividing the General Assembly into regional sections to avoid complicating the establishment of a strong international organization. Regarding the Mexico City Conference, the government intends to discuss the Dumbarton Oaks proposals without making inconsistent commitments. For the proposed International Court of Justice, it is recommended that a meeting of fifteen jurists be convened immediately to prepare a statute and implementation procedures for the United Nations Conference.

UNC Chapel Hill placed associate professor Dwayne Dixon on leave to investigate allegations of "politically motivated violence" following social media posts linking him to the Redneck Revolt and flyers posted at Georgetown University. While right-wing activists called for his firing, the American Association of University Professors condemned the university's actions, stating Dixon's involvement in the now-inactive group was being used to fuel unsubstantiated rumors.

Three Illinois gang members were shot and killed at point-blank range during an auto racing event at Great Lakes Dragaway near Union Grove, Wis., on Aug. 13, 2017. Authorities are searching for a suspect described as a thin, athletic Black man.

Stan Bowman and coach Quenneville discussed the team's progress, noting the development of goaltender Corey Crawford and player Bryan Bickell. Bowman emphasized the importance of organizational consistency and team effort in achieving success, while Quenneville focused on playing to the team's strengths and managing the upcoming matchup against a mobile, skilled opponent.

The Bearish Engulfing candlestick pattern is a technical analysis tool used to identify potential trend reversals from an uptrend to a downtrend. It consists of a bullish candlestick followed by a larger bearish candlestick that completely engulfs the first candle's body. While it indicates strong bearish sentiment, it does not guarantee a reversal and can produce false signals. Traders can improve accuracy and confirm validity by using other indicators like RSI or MACD, monitoring market momentum, and considering the broader market context. In the stock market, the pattern has a reported success rate between 55% and 65%.

The 50 EMA strategy is a technical analysis trend-following method that uses the 50-day exponential moving average to identify medium-term trends and generate buy and sell signals. Traders often combine the 50 EMA with indicators like the RSI or MACD to confirm signals, typically entering long positions when the price is above the EMA and short positions when it is below. While backtests of simple moving average crossover systems showed varying results across assets, using the 50 EMA as a filter alongside a second indicator produced improved annual returns and lower maximum drawdowns for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100.

The AMD Secure RNG library provides an API to access hardware-generated random values via x86 RDRAND and RDSEED instructions. The library abstracts low-level programming, manages hardware failure checks, and allows users to request single values or streams of 16, 32, or 64-bit random numbers and bytes. It includes APIs to check for hardware support using the CPUID instruction. While hardware-based generation via memory-mapped I/O is slower than software-based PRNGs, the library can be used to seed PRNGs for improved performance in latency-sensitive applications.

A federal appeals court granted a request to stay an injunction, allowing the Education Department to proceed with a reduction-in-force plan to fire half of the 550 employees at its Office for Civil Rights.

In response to threats from the Trump administration, liberal nonprofits are preparing for potential investigations and legal battles. Following the murder of Charlie Kirk, administration officials and Republican lawmakers have targeted nonprofit organizations, specifically accusing them of funding "Antifa" and radical movements. In response, some nonprofits are considering radical measures such as relocating outside the U.S., re-registering as businesses to forfeit 501(c)(3) status, or merging to survive. Carolina Herrera has hired Lisa Arnold as vice president of retail and Thea Terenik as vice president of global merchandising. Both New York-based executives report to president Emilie Rubinfeld.

British shares fell on Thursday, with the FTSE 100 down 0.6 percent as investors reacted to Federal Reserve minutes indicating potential balance sheet shrinkage. Financials, including Lloyds and RBS, led the decline, while Pearson dropped 8.9 percent following an Exane downgrade. Conversely, real estate, mining, and Tullow Oil saw gains.

U.S. manufacturing faces a shortage of qualified workers for automated and advanced technology roles. While hundreds of thousands of jobs are open, they require specialized skills and education that many displaced workers lack.

This pre-posttest study analyzed the effect of enforcing the 2014 Kenya Health Sector Referral Guidelines at Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) on orthopaedic and trauma facility referrals. Following enforcement on July 1, 2021, there was a significant reduction in direct referrals from Tier II and III health facilities to KNH, alongside an increase in referrals from Tiers IV, V, and VI. Approximately 43 facilities ceased referring directly to KNH, with over two-thirds being private facilities. Major factors associated with referrals included human resource capacity, infrastructure, medical supplies, financial considerations, and patient preference.

The 1-2-2 zone is a defense effective against outside shooting, fast breaking, and protecting leads. It features a point at the top, wings at the elbows, and baseline players above the blocks. Defenders shift based on ball position, with specific responsibilities for the point, wings, and baseline players. Variations include wing corner shifts, corner traps, switching to a 2-1-2 zone, and extending into a press.

Emory University researchers found that the probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) may protect the liver from oxidative damage caused by acetaminophen. In mice, an LGG-rich diet improved the liver's antioxidant response via the protein Nrf2, though further studies are required to determine if these results replicate in humans.

On March 28, 2001, Enron CEO Jeff Skilling attributed the company's declining share price to "multiple compression" and a market trend away from high price-to-earnings ratio stocks. While analysts noted Enron-specific issues, such as broadband valuation and news regarding its Dabhol power plant, Skilling maintained that the company's current multiple is sustainable. Additionally, Enron's 2000 performance resulted in significant bonuses for executives, including $7 million for chairman Kenneth Lay and $5.6 million for Skilling.

Despite global education expansion, significant shortfalls in participation, quality, and equality existed by 2020, as outlined by the Sustainable Development Goals and the Incheon Declaration. The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated these deficiencies by causing widespread school closures and shifting toward distance learning, which disproportionately affected disadvantaged students. However, the pandemic also forced the education sector to embrace technology. The author argues that the field of Comparative and International Education must address its own scholarly deficiencies—such as Northern hegemony and the "black box" syndrome—to investigate pandemic-related changes and help build better education systems to reach the 2030 goals.

Edgar D. Closson sought to foreclose a material man’s lien against Marie E. Billman for lumber used in a construction project. The defendants argued that the appellant, who signed a bond for the contractor, was a guarantor liable for the unpaid materials because the contractor failed to deliver the building free of liens, as required by the contract. The court affirmed the judgment, ruling that the bond and contract must be construed together, making the guarantor liable for the contractor's failure to pay for materials.

NVIDIA's new shading advancements include mesh shading, which improves geometry processing efficiency and object capacity by moving processing to the GPU. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows dynamic shading rate control to improve frame rates through content, motion, or foveated adaptive shading. Texture-space shading enables caching and reusing shading results in a private coordinate space. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) extends Single Pass Stereo by allowing multiple views with different origins or directions to be rendered in a single pass.

The disclosure relates to systems and methods for route planning for vehicles, such as automatic guided vehicles (AGVs), using a map (e.g., a topological map). The process involves obtaining a map, determining a vehicle's start location and destination, and obtaining motion status information of other vehicles in the region. A modified map is generated by adjusting node information—such as weight values, passability, or turn capability—based on the motion status of other vehicles to avoid collisions. Route planning is then performed by determining total costs for nodes between the start and destination nodes using the modified map.

The U.S. strategy for 1983 involves maintaining high standards for arms control (INF and START), applying diplomatic pressure on regional issues like Afghanistan and southern Africa, and pursuing human rights through private diplomacy. Economic relations must not subsidize Soviet military power, while bilateral relations should seek mutual benefits and broader societal access. Dialogue should be structured through four levels—summitry, ministerial contacts, ambassadors, and departmental specialists—to protect security interests while incentivizing Soviet cooperation.

The Supreme Court affirmed that a discharged bankrupt has no standing to appeal a court's refusal to stay a writ of execution levied on real estate conveyed to his wife, as the order does not affect his rights. Questions regarding the bank's right to proceed or the validity of the sale under the Bankruptcy Act must be raised by the wife rather than the appellant.

Delta Insurance is expanding its presence in the South Island's booming technology sector by providing various liability, technology, and cyber insurance products. To better serve the region, the company has appointed Karl Samson, an experienced liability underwriter, and joined Canterbury Tech.
A study shows that adding four live ants to warmed cow's milk acidifies and thickens it into yogurt, a traditional method once popular in Bulgaria and Turkey.

MacKenzie Scott is continuing her commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion through large, unrestricted donations to scholarship providers and HBCU endowments. Recent contributions include a gift to 10,000 Degrees, tens of millions to Native Forward, and $70 million to UNCF to bolster endowments for 37 HBCUs. Over the past five years, Scott has donated more than $19 billion, utilizing a trust-based model of rapid, flexible grants to support underrepresented learners and various social causes.

Under the leadership of Commissioner Lisa Baird, the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) navigated the COVID-19 pandemic by implementing a phased return-to-play protocol. This resulted in the 2020 Challenge Cup, a tournament held in a controlled "bubble" in Utah, and a subsequent Fall Series. Despite the pandemic, the league saw increased television viewership, new sponsorship deals, and expansion through new teams like Angel City FC. As the league enters its next decade, it faces challenges regarding brand redevelopment, fan engagement, and negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement.

Cu-doped NiO thin films were synthesized using an ultra-fast spray pyrolysis technique with a 1.5-minute deposition time. Structural analysis via XRD and Raman spectroscopy confirmed successful Cu incorporation, characterized by lattice expansion, reduced crystallite size, and vibrational mode shifts. Optical characterization showed a reduction in the bandgap from 3.70 eV to 3.65 eV and increased visible-light absorbance. Electrical and gas-sensing evaluations revealed that Cu-doped NiO films exhibit higher sensitivity to LPG compared to undoped NiO, attributed to improved charge transport and increased surface reactivity.

On November 13, 2017, Apple Inc. completed the issuance and sale of several series of senior unsecured notes totaling $6 billion in aggregate principal amount, with maturities ranging from 2019 to 2047.

The provided text details the AGESATM software architecture, focusing on initialization processes, PEI/DXE drivers, and host environment requirements. Key components include:

* **Initialization & PPIs:** Various Protocol Interface Implementations (PPIs) manage processor core and memory initialization, such as `AMD_PEI_INIT_EARLY_PPI_GUID` and `AMD_MEM_INIT_PPI_GUID`.
* **PEIMs & DXE Drivers:** PEIMs handle post-reset duties and memory initialization, while DXE drivers perform late initialization and supply system information via data tables and protocols like `AgesaDxeProtocol`.
* **Memory & Stack Management:** The text describes procedures for establishing and removing pre-memory stacks (Cache-As-RAM), managing memory range descriptors, and handling system memory availability.
* **Build & Configuration:** AGESATM supports "Binary Modules" and "Source Integration" build methods. Configuration is managed via `<Plat>Options.c` and various control files.
* **Call-outs & Services:** The host environment must implement required call-out functions for memory allocation (`AgesaAllocateBuffer`), system resets, and SPD data reading to ensure proper software operation.

Best Buy is offering $220 off the Lenovo Legion 7i Gen 10, bringing the price to $1,650. The laptop features a 2,560 x 1,600 OLED screen, an RTX 5060 GPU, and a keyboard with a numpad. Battery life lasted less than five hours during video playback tests.

To sustain operations without a paywall, The Jerusalem Post is asking readers for $5 a month to receive an ad-free experience, premium content, a Hebrew learning magazine, Jerusalem Report content, and an ePaper.
On February 1, 2018, Amazon.com, Inc. announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and year ended December 31, 2017.

Alek Minassian, 25, has been charged with 10 counts of first-degree murder after driving a rental van into pedestrians in Toronto. While the attack killed 10 people and injured 15, officials stated it does not represent a national security threat.

The U.S. Transportation Department reported that last year, airlines achieved record-low rates for flight cancellations, passenger bumping, and mishandled luggage. Additionally, on-time arrivals increased to 81.4 percent, and passenger complaints decreased by 11.3 percent compared to 2015.

Improving farmers' conditions requires broad education, organizational cooperation, and government assistance through the Department of Agriculture. While farmers must lead their own efforts, the government supports them via associations, specialized agricultural education, and policies like irrigation and forest preservation. Additionally, the text recommends constructing a memorial amphitheater at Arlington and granting Congress authority over marriage, divorce, and polygamy to ensure national welfare.

Scientists at Oregon Health & Science University reported that their attempt to create human eggs using somatic cell nuclear transfer has been mostly unsuccessful. While the technique has shown progress, such as developing "mitomeiosis" to reduce chromosome numbers, it requires further refinement before clinical testing.

A study suggests that the brain chemical dopamine plays a role in the development of the mother-child bond. Researchers found that mothers secreted more dopamine when watching videos of their own babies, and those who secreted more were more likely to provide optimal care and be sensitive to their infants' needs.

Trauma and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) can negatively impact the academic performance, mental health, and social engagement of post-secondary students, including those in occupational therapy (OT) programs. To address these challenges, the paper explores the Trauma-Informed Care (TIC) framework, which utilizes six core principles—safety, trustworthiness, peer support, collaboration, empowerment, and cultural respect—to create supportive learning environments. The authors review SAMHSA’s implementation domains and suggest various educational strategies for OT educators, such as providing advance notice of triggering content, incorporating self-care, and utilizing simulation-based training. Implementing TIC in health professions education aims to mitigate academic barriers and improve student retention and well-being.

The June 8, 2001, issue of CongressDailyAM reports that the House Appropriations Committee has developed FY02 subcommittee spending allocations that largely follow President Bush's requests, though some differ by billions of dollars. House leadership intends to adhere to the president's $6.1 billion FY01 defense supplemental recommendation despite opposition from some members. Additionally, House Republicans suggest the Democratic takeover of the Senate will not significantly alter House partisan relations, while Rep. Steve Largent announced his intention to resign his Oklahoma seat in November to run for governor. Other reports include FDA warnings regarding mailed prescription drugs, discussions on drug patent reform, and EU concerns regarding a U.S. steel investigation.

AMC Entertainment faces potential shareholder dilution from a proposal to double authorized shares to 1.1 billion. The company maintains over $3 billion in net debt, experienced weak Q3 box office revenues, and trades at a discount to peer CNK due to losses, negative equity, and cash burn.

Robert Stuart has presented evidence questioning the authenticity of the BBC Panorama documentary “Saving Syria’s Children.” The investigation highlights discrepancies regarding the reality of alleged injuries, inconsistent victim counts from various sources, and significant disparities in the reported timing of the event. Additionally, the work notes the political backgrounds and connections of medical personnel featured in the footage.

This study uses an individual-based mathematical model to assess the global risk of *pfhrp2/3* gene deletions, which cause false-negative results in HRP2-based malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs). The researchers developed two risk scores: an "Innate Risk Score," measuring a region's potential for deletions to spread based on transmission intensity and treatment-seeking data, and a "Prospective Risk Score," which incorporates current deletion prevalence to predict future spread. Findings indicate that malaria prevalence is the primary driver of deletion selection, with the highest risks identified in low-transmission regions. In Africa, the model predicts significant spread from the Horn of Africa through East Africa, identifying several high-risk countries, including Eritrea, Ethiopia, Djibouti, Senegal, Zambia, and Kenya. The study provides an interactive tool to help policymakers prioritize surveillance and the deployment of alternative RDTs.

Researchers used a technique combining somatic cell nuclear transfer, fertilization, and the molecule roscovitine to coax human skin cells into expelling half their chromosomes. This proof-of-concept allowed the cells to become functional eggs capable of forming early human embryos. While the resulting embryos were not viable due to abnormal chromosome numbers, the breakthrough may eventually help treat infertility.

The lecture explores protein folding through a mechanical model of fixed-angle linkages, where the protein backbone is treated as a chain with fixed edge lengths and angles. The professor discusses several mathematical problems related to these linkages:

*   **Span:** Determining the maximum and minimum distance between endpoints. Finding the minimum or maximum span for flat configurations is NP-hard, though the 3D maximization problem remains open.
*   **Flattening:** Determining if a linkage can exist in a 2D plane without self-intersection, a problem also identified as NP-hard.
*   **Flat State Connectivity:** Investigating if all possible flat configurations of a chain belong to the same connected component.
*   **Locked Chains:** Identifying configurations that cannot move despite having degrees of freedom.

The professor introduces the concept of "producible protein chains," modeling the ribosome as a cone that constrains the protein as it is synthesized. He presents a theorem stating that any chain produced by such a cone is in a single connected component and is flat-state connected. This is demonstrated using a "canonical configuration" (an alpha CCC) and a "momento method" to show that producible chains can be algorithmically moved between states, providing a potential mechanical model for how nature achieves efficient protein folding.

The Securities and Exchange Commission has launched a preliminary inquiry into whether energy consultants advising Governor Gray Davis used inside information to trade power company stocks. This follows the firing of five consultants for potential conflicts of interest and disclosures that Davis' press secretary, Steve Maviglio, also purchased Calpine Corp. stock. Additionally, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's decision to limit electricity refunds to approximately $4 billion—less than the state's $9 billion request—has prompted plans for an appeal. Meanwhile, the Davis administration continues to seek a legislative bailout for Southern California Edison.

Gas colic is a common condition caused by gas buildup in the large colon, which can lead to complications like intestinal twisting. Primary causes include inadequate forage consumption, stall confinement, stress, and rapid changes in diet. To reduce risk, horses should have constant access to forage, increased movement, and gradual transitions when introducing new feeds.

Newark Public Safety Director Anthony F. Ambrose released photos of nine suspects involved in seven unsolved crimes dating back to 2016. The incidents include shootings and armed robberies, and officials are seeking public assistance to locate the suspects.

The Asus Zenfone 5Z has launched in India in Meteor Silver and Midnight Blue, available exclusively on Flipkart starting July 15. The flagship features a 6.2-inch display, Snapdragon 845 SoC, and three storage variants priced between Rs. 29,999 and Rs. 36,999.

The Michigan Supreme Court affirmed the conviction of Richard L. Helzer for gross indecency but reversed the Court of Appeals' order for a new trial on all charges. The Court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing provision rather than a penalty enhancement. Consequently, to avoid prejudice, a defendant must be tried by a separate jury for the sexual delinquency charge unless they waive a jury trial. While the defendant is entitled to 20 peremptory challenges for the sexual delinquency jury due to the potential for life imprisonment, they are only entitled to challenges appropriate to the principal charge when the initial jury is empaneled. The Court remanded the case for a hearing before a separately empaneled jury regarding the sexual delinquency charge.

On March 27, 2017, underwriters for Tesla, Inc.’s 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due March 15, 2022, exercised their option to purchase an additional $127.5 million in principal amount of the notes. The NVIDIA Turing architecture introduces several advancements in GPU performance and rendering. To manage attacks, experts suggest writing down reassuring facts or mantras, visualizing the panic as a passing wave, using smartphone games or music for distraction, and practicing daily deep breathing exercises.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU features 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and 40 MB of L2 cache. The architecture includes third-generation Tensor Cores, Compute Data Compression, and Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability, which allows a single GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU Instances. This lecture covers various web security vulnerabilities and defenses. The professor demonstrates the Shellshock bug, where malformed HTTP headers can execute arbitrary Bash commands, and cross-site scripting (XSS), where attackers inject malicious scripts into web pages. Defenses discussed include browser-based XSS filters, HTTP-only cookies, privilege separation via separate domains, content sanitization (e.g., Django's template system), and Content Security Policy (CSP).

The lecture also addresses SQL injection, where untrusted input manipulates database queries, and suggests rigorous data encoding as a solution. Regarding session management, the professor explains stateless cookies using Message Authentication Codes (MACs) and alternatives like DOM storage and client-side certificates. Finally, the lecture explores protocol vulnerabilities, such as URL parsing inconsistencies, the GIFAR attack (embedding JAR files in GIFs), and covert channel attacks (CSS-based, cache-based, DNS-based, and rendering-based) used to sniff user browsing history.

A study by Royal Holloway University of London found that bumblebee queens exposed to traces of the neonicotinoid pesticide thiamethoxam were 26 percent less likely to lay eggs. The lecture covers graphical realizations of Reed-Muller codes, specifically focusing on Hadamard transform realizations. The professor explains that while cycle-free realizations (like trellises) are more complex, they allow for exact decoding, whereas realizations with cycles are simpler but result in sub-optimal decoding. 

The discussion transitions to the sum-product algorithm, a method for A Posteriori Probability (APP) decoding. On cycle-free graphs, the algorithm provides exact decoding by utilizing a past-future decomposition, where the probability of a state variable is calculated by multiplying information from the past and future components of the graph. The professor notes that in graphs with cycles, the algorithm becomes an iterative, approximate method.

Researchers used deep learning to develop a neuroimaging biomarker for multiple sclerosis (MS) by modeling disease duration (DD) from structural brain MRI scans. The Situation Calculus is a logical language used in artificial intelligence to reason about dynamical systems. Traded on the Cboe Futures Exchange, these contracts allow participants to speculate on volatility, hedge market risk, and diversify portfolios. Researchers developed a simultaneous ADF-EDS-EELS tomography approach to achieve 3D nanoscale mapping of structure, chemical composition, and valence states in a single, low-dose acquisition. Developed by Ralph Nelson Elliott, the Elliott Wave theory is a technical analysis principle stating that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns. The theory classifies waves into two types: impulse waves, which move in the direction of the trend through five sub-waves, and corrective waves, which move opposite to the trend through three sub-waves. Used by various traders in stock, forex, and commodity markets, the theory helps identify potential price directions, though its highly subjective nature makes it difficult to backtest.

Justices are debating whether the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act is criminal or civil to determine if its application to Holsey Ellingburg violates the ex post facto clause. While the government and Ellingburg's counsel argue the statute cannot increase his punishment, some justices questioned if the restitution is penal, while others suggested its inclusion in criminal sentencing makes it penal in nature.

This research explores the relationship between microtubule (MT) dynamics and drug resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The study utilizes computational analysis of EB1 comet tracking to monitor MT polymerization and identifies that AR splice variants, such as ARv7, correlate with increased MT dynamicity and taxane resistance. The authors propose using MT dynamics signatures in patient-derived organoids to predict drug efficacy. Additionally, the text examines how the GSK3β-pVHL axis regulates MT homeostasis and quiescence, noting that phosphorylation of pVHL by GSK3β increases MT turnover. The findings suggest that targeting the tubulin transcriptome or modulating MT-regulating proteins could serve as a strategy to sensitize resistant prostate tumors to therapy.

Price action trading is a form of technical analysis that uses historical price movement patterns, such as chart and candlestick patterns, to determine trade entry and exit points. Unlike other technical analysis, pure price action focuses on price movements alone, studying swing highs, swing lows, and market sentiment with little to no indicator input. Day trading price action strategies can be discretionary or quantitative and may include trend following, breakouts, reversals, or scalping. Because price action patterns can be difficult to code, the text emphasizes the importance of quantifying and backtesting strategies using historical data to ensure effectiveness and avoid cognitive biases.

In this lecture, William Green reviews stochastic methods, focusing on the application and limitations of three primary computational tools:

* **Metropolis Monte Carlo:** Used for evaluating multidimensional integrals by utilizing weighting factors. Green emphasizes the importance of choosing appropriate step sizes to ensure efficient sampling and warns that improper step sizes can lead to repetitive states or failure to cover the entire space.
* **Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC):** Employed for systems with massive state spaces, such as catalytic surfaces, where probability distributions are non-stationary. He discusses the Gillespie algorithm and suggests techniques like accelerating fast processes or ignoring irrelevant low-probability events to improve computational efficiency.
* **Molecular Dynamics (MD):** Solves equations of motion to simulate physical time scales. While MD provides time-accurate data, it is limited by very small time steps (femtoseconds), making it unsuitable for observing slow processes occurring on millisecond scales.

Green concludes by advising that researchers must select the specific tool that matches their problem's time scale and objectives rather than using a familiar method inappropriately.

Russ Tedrake discusses model-free optimal control, comparing policy gradient methods with value function methods. Policy gradient methods scale well to high dimensions and offer guaranteed convergence but can suffer from high variance and require smoothness. Value function methods are often more data-efficient but can struggle with convergence or diverge due to policy oscillations.

The actor-critic approach combines these methods by representing both a policy (the actor) and a value estimate (the critic). This combination aims to provide the stability of policy gradients with the efficiency of value methods. Tedrake illustrates this using a case study of "Toddler," an underactuated walking robot. Using an actor-critic algorithm, the robot learned to stabilize its gait and adapt to different terrains and even mechanical failures within minutes, demonstrating the effectiveness of model-free learning on real-world hardware.

The lecture discusses the complexities of wireless communication compared to wireline systems. While wireline communication primarily deals with white Gaussian noise, wireless communication is affected by fading caused by physical mechanisms like Doppler shifts and multipath interference.

The professor explains that in free space, electromagnetic field strength decreases as 1/r due to spherical radiation. When a receiver moves, it experiences a Doppler shift, which is a frequency change proportional to the vehicle's velocity relative to the speed of light. While a single Doppler shift can be tracked by frequency recovery systems, multiple paths with different Doppler shifts cause "fast fading" or multipath fading. This occurs because different signal paths have varying attenuations and propagation delays, creating a time-varying system.

The lecture concludes that wireless channels are best modeled as linear time-varying filters. The stability of the system depends on the Doppler spread—the difference between the largest and smallest Doppler shifts—which determines how frequently the channel characteristics must be re-measured.

The lecture discusses the combinatorial bounds and algorithms for folding polygons into convex polyhedra using gluing trees. The professor explains that while general gluings can be infinite due to "rolling belts," they can be made finite by considering combinatorial types. 

Key points include:
* **Complexity:** For general gluings, the number of combinatorial types is exponential ($2^{\Theta(n)}$). For "bounded sharpness" polygons (where reflex angles are bounded away from 360 degrees), the number of gluings and the algorithms to list them are polynomial.
* **Algorithms:** An edge-to-edge gluing case can be solved in polynomial time using dynamic programming to decide if a folding exists. For general gluings, an exponential-time enumeration algorithm exists.
* **Examples:** The professor demonstrates these concepts using a cross (which can form 85 different gluings resulting in 23 distinct polyhedra) and an equilateral triangle.

The lecture discusses renormalization and the summation of logarithms within Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET), specifically focusing on the $b \to s \gamma$ decay. The professor explains how ultraviolet divergences in the effective theory are handled using counterterms to achieve matching between the full theory and SCET. 

Key concepts include:
* **Sudakov Logarithms:** The emergence of Sudakov double logarithms from the renormalization group evolution of Wilson coefficients.
* **Anomalous Dimensions:** The distinction between regular anomalous dimensions and the "cusp" anomalous dimension, which is associated with the kink in Wilson lines.
* **Renormalization Group (RG) Evolution:** The process of summing leading logs (LL), next-to-leading logs (NLL), and higher orders by solving differential equations for the Wilson coefficients.
* **Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS):** The application of SCET to DIS, demonstrating how hard-collinear factorization separates hard fluctuations from colinear degrees of freedom (the proton). This process leads to the derivation of operators that define Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and reproduces classical evolution equations like DGLAP.

Yael Kalai discusses probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs) and their construction from the GKR protocol. The AMD Geode CS5535 Silicon Revision A3 contains several technical issues:

*   **SSMI/IRQ:** Simultaneous IRQ and SSMI events may cause the SSMI to signal after the I/O completes, making SSMIs unreliable.
*   **UDMA/PIO:** Enabling the IDE bus master before sending a PIO command packet causes UDMA transactions to fail.
*   **ACPI S3:** GPIO[27:24] transitions (SLP_BUT#, THRM_ALRM#, and LOW_BAT#) do not function as wake events from the S3 state.
*   **RTC CMOS RAM:** Reading the legacy data port immediately after writing to the extended data port can return incorrect data.
*   **LPC DMA:** Block and demand mode legacy DMA to LPC can block I/O cycles and return invalid data.
*   **USB Controllers:** Clock gating can cause register read failures when controllers are idle.
*   **ATAC:** Using WORD-aligned PRD sizes can cause the ATAC to hang; DWORD alignment is required.
*   **SMB Controller:** The NEGACK status bit may not set immediately when accessing non-existing devices.
*   **GPIO:** Atomic writes to High Bank Feature Bit Registers may clear non-selected bits after a suspend.
*   **Sleep State:** If delay counters are larger than the PM_SED delay, SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y may not de-assert during transitions out of Sleep.

Ulysses S. Gandy appealed his second manslaughter conviction following a two-car collision that killed three people. Gandy challenged the trial court's refusal of specific jury instructions, the admission of sketches as evidence, and the lack of a jury recess for refreshments. Researchers developed a meta-population model to investigate how Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR) relate to SARS-CoV-2 transmission dynamics. The model incorporates GCMR data from four settings—retail and recreation, grocery and pharmacy, transit stations, and workplaces—alongside multiplicative factors for seasonality (temperature) and virus variants (Alpha and Delta). 

Applied to Norway, Sweden, and German regions (Bavaria and Berlin), the model found that GCMR data reflect population behavior changes linked to infection dynamics. In Sweden, the GCMR settings accounted for 60% of infections, while in Norway, they accounted for 39%. In Norway and Sweden, transit and workplace settings were identified as the most important for transmission at baseline activity levels, whereas in the German regions, retail and recreation contributed most. The model also estimated that a 20°C temperature increase reduces transmissibility by approximately 40%.

This study used EEG to investigate neural noise in 19 adults with Tourette syndrome (TS) compared to 19 healthy controls by measuring responses to median nerve electrical stimulation. Results showed that the TS group exhibited increased trial-by-trial variability in somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) magnitude and flatter 1/f noise curves at beta and gamma frequencies. While the timing and topography of early-to-mid-latency SEPs were largely similar between groups, the TS group showed a significantly increased P2 (P100) component amplitude, which correlated with tic impairment. Additionally, the TS group demonstrated reduced alpha-band phase coherence following stimulation. The findings suggest that while neuronal sensorimotor recruitment is less stable at rest in individuals with TS, this variability normalizes in response to stimulation.

This study addresses the challenge of capturing dynamic events in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) process modeling by identifying and extracting reusable Ontology Design Patterns (ODPs). They surveyed several ontologies, including PMDcore, P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, OPMW, WILD, and GPO, to identify patterns aligning with these requirements. Additionally, the authors proposed and evaluated a baseline method for the automatic extraction of ODPs using semantic similarity techniques and the ROBOT framework. Evaluation results indicated that P-PLAN achieved high precision for process and resource ODPs, while PMDcore was the only ontology to support all three requirement categories.

Devised by E.S.C. Coppock in 1965, the Coppock Curve is a long-term momentum indicator used to identify significant market swings. It is calculated as a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of 11-month and 14-month rate-of-change indicators. The strategy triggers long entries when the curve crosses above the zero line and exits when it crosses below. A backtest of the strategy on a monthly S&P 500 chart showed 12 trades since 1960, resulting in a risk-adjusted return exceeding a buy & hold strategy and a substantial reduction in drawdown.

This work proposes a theoretical framework that integrates behavioral framing effects into the Bayesian persuasion model of information design. While traditional models focus on quantitative correlations in signaling, this research incorporates how linguistic framing—such as text, phrasing, and non-textual cues—shapes a receiver's beliefs. 

The authors identify three optimization variants: recommendation-only, framing-only, and joint optimization of both. Theoretical analysis reveals that while framing-only optimization is computationally hard (NP-hard) and sensitive to errors, joint optimization is more tractable, continuous, and amenable to approximation. Using Large Language Models (LLMs) as "belief oracles" to proxy human behavior, the authors implement a hill-climbing approach. Empirical case studies involving a realtor and a clothing brand demonstrate the efficacy of this method, with results showing directional alignment with human subject evaluations.

The adapter pattern uses a container to modify an application container's interface to meet predefined standards, such as consistent monitoring or logging. Multi-node distributed patterns include:
* **Replicated Load-Balanced Services:** Stateless services are replicated and distributed via a load balancer to provide redundancy and scale.
* **Session Tracked Services:** An adaptation of the replicated pattern that ensures specific users are routed to the same replica, often using consistent hashing.
* **Sharded Services:** Used for stateful services where data is too large for one machine; each shard serves a subset of requests.
* **Replicated, Sharded Caches:** Combines replication and sharding to ensure cache shards are resilient to failures and can be scaled.
* **Scatter/Gather Pattern:** Achieves parallelism by distributing a single request to all leaf nodes, which return partial results to a root node for combination.
* **Functions and Event-Driven Processing (FaaS):** Provides granular, stateless, and automatically scaled computing. Patterns include the **Decorator Pattern** for request/response transformation and **Handling Events** for asynchronous, decoupled tasks like two-factor authentication.

The discussion transitions from continuous solutions to numerical methods:

This patent application describes methods and systems for improving ladar (laser radar) technology, specifically focusing on optimizing the "gaze" or dwell time of scanning transmitters on regions of interest. 

Key innovations include:
* **Field Splitting and Inversion:** Using an optical field splitter/inverter (such as a W-shaped reflector or a triangular prism) to redirect laser pulses. This technique inverts the scan pattern so that the naturally faster portion of a resonant scan occurs at the edges of the field of view, while the slower portion resides in the center, increasing dwell time in critical areas.
* **Induced Periodic Phase Drift:** Applying a time-varying phase drift to Lissajous scan patterns. This method uses a total least squares approach to reduce scan gaps and blind spots in desired regions without reducing the overall revisit rate.
* **Ellipsoidal Reimaging:** Utilizing an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector (ECR) assembly between two scanning mirrors. This allows for a compact beam scanner design using two small, equally sized mirrors by reimaging the beam, which increases scan speed and field of view while minimizing distortions.

Molecular Dynamics (MD) uses the Green-Kubo (GK) and Non-Equilibrium MD (NEMD) methods to calculate thermal conductivity. While NEMD is straightforward, the GK method in LAMMPS originally used a heat flux formula valid only for pair potentials, potentially leading to incorrect results for many-body interactions. This work implements the Torii et al. formulas in LAMMPS to enable exact heat flux calculations for both control volumes and control surfaces, including the Spectral Decomposition of the Heat Current (SDHC), for arbitrary many-body potentials.

COPD is a leading cause of death in the U.S. caused almost exclusively by smoking. Symptoms include chronic coughing and shortness of breath. Diagnosis involves a pulmonary function test, and treatments like inhalers, oxygen, or pulmonary rehabilitation can manage symptoms and slow decline. This qualitative study evaluated distance education in Turkish sports higher education during the COVID-19 pandemic through interviews with 14 lecturers. Findings identified positive aspects such as time and space flexibility, technological opportunities, and resource access. Conversely, negative aspects included communication issues, motivation problems, inequality of opportunity, and the difficulty of conducting applied sports lessons. Challenges centered on infrastructure deficiencies and assessment difficulties, while management was viewed as lacking unity and effective crisis response. The study concludes that while distance education is a necessary alternative, improvements in infrastructure, data security, and field-specific implementation are required to prevent learning losses.

This study uses first-principles calculations to investigate the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) composed of Mn3Sn(01$\bar{1}$0) electrodes and an MgO(110) barrier. The results show a TMR ratio exceeding 1000%. The TMR effect is attributed to the momentum-dependent spin splitting in Mn3Sn—specifically the x-component of spin polarization—and the electron filtering properties of the MgO barrier.

The MSPM0G MCU features an ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU with various operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN) and two power domains (PD1 and PD0). Peripherals include GPIO, IOMUX, dual 12-bit ADCs, a temperature sensor, VREF, a comparator (COMP), a 12-bit DAC, and various communication interfaces (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD). Additional features include a math accelerator (MATHACL), a Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS) with an RTC and watchdog, and multiple timer instances.

This bibliometric study analyzes academic research on "Digital Accessibility" and "Digital Accessibility in Education" using the Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC databases from 2013 to 2024. This study evaluated a streamlined workflow for analyzing and reporting Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) data using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software in hematologic malignancies. Testing ten myeloid malignancy cases, the study found that OGM via VIA detected all variants identified by standard of care (SOC) methods, such as karyotyping and FISH, while also identifying additional reportable findings in 87.5% of positive cases. Technologist review times averaged between 20 and 45 minutes for non-complex cases. The researchers concluded that the OGM and VIA workflow provides an efficient, high-resolution, and objective approach for interpreting and reporting cytogenomic variants.

This paper examines the normative assumptions of educational disparity studies through the lens of luck egalitarianism. While luck egalitarianism justifies correcting disparities caused by "brute luck" (uncontrollable factors), the author uses Elizabeth Anderson’s critiques—the harshness and humiliation objections—to highlight its limitations. To address these, the paper proposes incorporating three additional values: fresh start, sufficiency, and respect. The author concludes that empirical research on educational disparities should expand beyond fairness to investigate these values, suggesting specific research directions such as longitudinal data analysis, academic achievement thresholds, and the study of student humiliation in classrooms.

This study reviewed a large cohort of over 18,000 plasma samples from more than 15,000 patients to evaluate the performance of the Karius Test, an mcfDNA sequencing platform. The MMA Manifesto’s Middleweight Rankings, voted on by a four-person panel, list Michael Bisping as number one, followed by Luke Rockhold, Yoel Romero, Chris Weidman (tied), Ronaldo ‘Jacare’ Souza (tied), Gegard Mousasi, Robert Whittaker, Anderson Silva, Vitor Belfort, and Kelvin Gastelum.

This study uses bibliometric analysis, including co-citation and co-word analyses of 402 Web of Science articles, to map the open education landscape. The research identifies five co-citation clusters: evolving open education, OER’s role, adoption of open education, MOOC educational paradigms, and OEP implementation. Co-word analysis reveals five emerging research themes: blended learning, openness during COVID-19, OER adoption challenges, inclusive digital pedagogy, and collaborative online academia. The findings highlight the transition from resource access to pedagogical practice and emphasize the need for institutional support and faculty development to overcome barriers to adoption and ensure equitable, sustainable access.

The OHL trading strategy is an intraday stock trading approach that uses the open, high, and low price levels from the first few minutes of a session to determine trade entries. A buy signal is generated if the open price equals the day's low, suggesting bullish sentiment, while a sell signal is generated if the open price equals the day's high, suggesting bearish sentiment. The strategy is best used on lower timeframes, such as 1-minute to 15-minute charts. Some traders combine OHL with Central Pivot Range (CPR) levels to refine entries. Backtests on the S&P 500 and WTI crude oil indicate that the opening price configuration can have predictive value for the day's direction.

This work introduces a novel neural solver that integrates physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with isogeometric analysis (IGA) to address challenges in applying PINNs to complex, multi-patch CAD geometries. The solver utilizes NN-based ansatz functions operating on the IGA reference domain to ensure solution continuity across patch interfaces, enable the strong imposition of Dirichlet boundary conditions via a custom output layer, and provide natural data normalization. The approach is rooted in the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) method and mortaring methods, employing a variational PINN framework to minimize a discretized energy functional. The method's efficacy is demonstrated through 2D magnetostatics and 3D nonlinear solid mechanics applications.

Starting in April, the Owen Sound Foodland in Georgian Bluffs will be one of 87 new stores authorized by the LCBO to sell beer and cider. The new 34,000-square-foot location, tentatively opening March 22, will expand existing departments, increase its workforce to approximately 160 employees, and feature a renewed focus on fresh products and expanded services.

Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) provide a computationally efficient alternative to Density Functional Theory (DFT). While graph-based equivariant neural networks (GNNs) are commonly used, they face challenges with point-defect computations due to computational demands and the importance of non-local interactions. To address this, the Accelerated Deep Atomic Potential Transformer (ADAPT) was developed. ADAPT is a coordinate-based Transformer that uses attention over all possible atom interactions to predict per-atom forces and energies. Trained on a DFT database of silicon defects, ADAPT outperforms pretrained universal MLFFs and demonstrates a training cost two orders of magnitude lower than message-passing architectures.

Nearly 88% of Ireland’s publicly-quoted companies met or exceeded earnings expectations, with an average earnings per share growth of 8%. While the Iseq index reached a 15-month high, it has underperformed other European markets due to Brexit concerns. Irish Continental Group is the top performer in the Iseq 10, while Aryzta has seen the largest share decline.

This study investigated the experiences, opinions, and suggestions of 2,371 parents regarding emergency distance education in Turkey during the COVID-19 pandemic. While 57.7% of parents viewed distance education positively for maintaining educational continuity and health safety, 42.3% expressed negative views, citing inadequacy and difficulty in adaptation. Key criticisms included technical infrastructure issues, insufficient content, and the inability of distance learning to replace face-to-face education. Findings highlighted that economic disparities exacerbated the digital divide, affecting internet access and device availability. Parents primarily used WhatsApp for teacher communication and suggested increasing lesson durations, enriching content, and implementing online assessments. The study concludes that distance education should serve as a support to, rather than a replacement for, face-to-face learning, and recommends improving technological infrastructure, digital literacy, and the adoption of open education philosophies to ensure equality of opportunity.

The Detroit Tigers, who used a closer by committee this season, have been linked to free agent closer Eugenio Suarez as a potential replacement. Suarez, who posted a 2.97 ERA and 40 saves this season, is expected to opt out of his contract this offseason.

The document also includes information regarding the UC Berkeley Business Plan Competition, the Big Game BBQ, and a Women in Leadership Conference.

The Executive Yuan plans to merge the Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission with the Ministry of Culture and the Mainland Affairs Council by the end of this year. Most staff will move to the Ministry of Culture, while six will transfer to the council. The decision follows a priority set by President Tsai Ing-wen to restructure the government. Prof. Mahesh Bandi has used turbulence theory and wind plant data to explain the statistical nature of wind power fluctuations. His research demonstrates that while geographically dispersed wind plants can average out power fluctuations at high frequencies, they exhibit correlated fluctuations at low frequencies due to shared long time-scale eddies. This discovery identifies a natural limit to "geographic smoothing," which can assist in estimating necessary energy reserves and informing optimal combinations of renewable energy sources for environmental policy.

Merger arbitrage seeks to profit from the price spread between a target company's stock and an acquisition offer. While successful deals yield returns, failed deals can cause significant losses. Backtesting shows that merger arbitrage funds, such as the IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF and The Merger Fund, exhibit lower volatility than the S&P 500 despite lower CAGRs. A Verdad Research study of deals from 2000 to 2020 found an 89% success rate and a 1.5% blended average return on long exposure.

Oxygen-containing rare-earth hydrides (REHO) are color-neutral photochromic materials suitable for smart window applications. Research on yttrium oxyhydride (YHO) films indicates that the photochromic transition involves two distinct processes: a fast decay occurring within the first few minutes, likely associated with local structural changes or hydrogen release, and a slow decay attributed to hydrogen migration and lattice contraction. A two-phase exponential decay model provides an accurate fit for the time-dependent optical transmittance of YHO under illumination.

This study investigated the degradation of commercial NMC/graphite coin cells cycled at 1C, 2C, and 3C rates. Results showed that 3C cycling caused the most significant capacity loss (~60.19%) and increased internal resistance. Structural analysis via XRD and SEM revealed cathode lattice contraction and surface decomposition, while the anode experienced interlayer expansion and surface roughness. Li-NRA measurements quantified a bulk lithium loss in the NMC cathode and a corresponding increase in lithium content in the graphite anode, indicating lithium trapping and plating. The study concludes that high C-rate cycling accelerates degradation through lithium inventory loss and structural damage.

The disclosed methods and systems utilize a cache coherent switch on chip, implemented via the Compute Express Link (CXL) interconnect, to enable low-latency memory access and resource sharing. The system allows for component disaggregation and server composability by providing cache coherency between various devices, such as accelerators, processors, and memory, without requiring a central processor to control all resource sharing. This architecture facilitates resource pooling—including memory, storage, and accelerators—across single servers, server racks, or networked data centers. Additionally, the switch on chip may include specialized modules for compression, security, and erasure coding, as well as a fabric manager to allocate and deallocate resources.

This study explores the (re)construction of professional identities in language teachers during their initial formation. The findings suggest that identity formation is a complex, non-chronological process involving the integration of student, intern, and teacher identities. The study highlights the importance of addressing the tension between academic theory and school practice to foster autonomous and reflexive professional identities.

The lecture covers the properties of coherent states, which are eigenstates of the annihilation operator and represent the closest quantum description to a classical electric field. The professor explains that coherent states are minimum uncertainty states, meaning they satisfy the Heisenberg uncertainty limit.

The discussion transitions to characterizing quantum states of light through quasi-probability distributions (Q, P, and Wigner) and photon number fluctuations. Key metrics include the Fano factor and the second-order temporal coherence function ($g^2$). While classical light must have $g^2 \geq 1$, non-classical states, such as Fock (number) states, can exhibit $g^2 < 1$. The professor highlights the importance of single-photon states for quantum computation and describes methods for their creation, such as using single atoms in high-finesse cavities or heralded single-photon sources using multiple atoms. Finally, the Hanbury Brown Twiss experiment is introduced as a method to distinguish between thermal and coherent light by measuring intensity correlations.

The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a district court's decision to dismiss the Chapter 7 bankruptcy case of Troy Edwin and Elaine Burris Tate for abuse. AMD created the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine to facilitate page migration, which involves copying page content and updating virtual-to-physical mappings to optimize performance in tiered memory systems. TMPM can off-load migration, pause DMA traffic to allow safe migration of active pages, and act as a trusted agent for migrating guest pages protected by Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) or Secure Nested Paging (SNP).

The engine supports moving groups of up to 128 pages via commands like PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO allows migration of pages that are concurrent targets of DMA operations, while PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST enables the migration of SNP-protected guest pages. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement. The TMPM firmware can be reloaded via the BIOS to PSP mailbox protocol, provided no operations are in flight and the ring buffer is torn down.

This paper introduces FoodSEM, an open-source large language model (LLM) fine-tuned for food named-entity linking (NEL). Using an instruction-response format, FoodSEM links food entity mentions to URIs from three ontologies: FoodOn, SNOMED-CT, and the Hansard taxonomy. The model was developed using a fine-tuning dataset created from the CafeteriaFCD and CafeteriaSA corpora, supplemented by artificially generated instances to balance entity distribution. Evaluation shows that FoodSEM achieves high macro-weighted F1 scores, reaching up to 98%, and significantly outperforms 0-shot, 1-shot, and 5-shot prompting baselines.

AMD created the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine to facilitate moving memory content between different performance tiers by copying page content and updating virtual-to-physical mappings. The TMPM can off-load page migration, pause DMA traffic during migration, and act as a trusted agent for migrating guest pages protected by Secure Nested Paging (SNP).

Key commands include:
* **PM_GET_CAPABILITIES**: Queries firmware version and capabilities.
* **PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO**: Migrates pages that may be concurrent targets of DMA operations, requiring IOMMU coordination.
* **PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST**: Migrates SNP guest pages, moving them from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid states to a Pre-Migration state.
* **PM_NOOP**: Marks the end of command strings.

The TMPM uses a ring buffer interface for asynchronous command processing, supporting multi-page commands of up to 128 entries for increased efficiency. All system physical addresses must be 4KB aligned. The engine requires IOMMU enablement and provides various interrupt sources for error handling and completion notification.

This course introduces Effective Field Theory (EFT), a framework used to focus on physics at specific scales by simplifying general theories, such as quantum field theory, into more computable forms. The course is divided into two halves: the first covers general EFT principles and ingredients, while the second focuses on soft-collinear effective theory.

EFTs are categorized into two approaches:
* **Top-down:** Starting with a known high-energy theory and integrating out heavy particles to construct a low-energy theory.
* **Bottom-up:** Constructing a low-energy theory based on symmetries, degrees of freedom, and power counting without necessarily knowing the high-energy theory.

Key concepts include power counting, which is essential for maintaining consistency and determining the expansion parameter, and the ability to correct descriptions to arbitrary precision through higher-order terms. The professor uses the Standard Model as an example of a bottom-up EFT, where higher-dimensional operators can describe physics beyond the current model.

This paper develops pseudospin models to describe the structure, ordering, and polarization switching of two phenyl-tetrazole (PHTZ) crystals: APHTZ and MPHTZ. 

For APHTZ, a canted ferroelectric, the model uses a two-sublattice Ising pseudospin formalism to represent proton tautomerism and $\pi$-bond switching. The model predicts a second-order phase transition and shows that a transverse electric field ($E_b$) induces a 90° rotation of the net polarization, transitioning the system from an FE-I to an FE-II phase via a tricritical point.

For MPHTZ, a uniaxial antiferroelectric, a four-sublattice model is employed. The model reproduces the field-induced transition from an AFE to an FE phase, characterized by double P-E hysteresis loops and a tricritical point. In both systems, the calculated switching fields are shown to be proportional to the spontaneous order parameter and intersublattice interaction constants.

The disclosed invention relates to a heterogeneous computing architecture featuring a multi-threaded, coarse-grained, self-scheduling, and reconfigurable computing fabric. The system utilizes a hybrid threading approach, employing both a synchronous mesh communication network to form pipelined synchronous domains and an asynchronous packet network for control signaling, memory access, and bridging domains. 

Individual computing units, or "tiles," consist of configurable computation circuits (including multiply-shift and arithmetic/logical/bit operation circuits), control circuitry, and configuration memory. The configuration memory includes a first instruction memory for data path instructions and a second "spoke" memory for selecting instructions, master synchronous inputs, and managing independent configuration. The control circuitry manages thread execution through mechanisms such as completion tables, loop tables, and various queues (continuation, reenter, priority, and run queues) to support ordered execution, conditional branching, and nested loops. The architecture is designed to provide high-performance, energy-efficient solutions for compute-intensive kernels like FFTs and FIR filters.

Researchers synthesized and investigated the exchange-disordered triangular magnet $\text{YbCu}_{1.14}\text{Se}_2$. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed a triangular lattice of $\text{Yb}^{3+}$ ions with non-ordered copper vacancies. Bulk measurements showed no magnetic ordering transition, sub-linear specific heat, and a frequency-dependent susceptibility peak at $T_f \approx 0.1\text{ K}$ characteristic of spin-glass freezing. The absence of a 1/3 magnetization plateau suggests a departure from the ideal 2D Heisenberg model, with the material's properties resembling the disordered ground state of $\text{YbMgGaO}_4$.

This paper proposes a new class of bivariate zero-inflated Poisson (BZIP) models designed to capture both excess zeros and varying dependence structures in multivariate count data. By incorporating a common inflation factor and leveraging comonotonic or counter-monotonic shocks, the model allows for both positive and negative correlations. Simulation studies demonstrate that likelihood-based methods generally outperform the method of moments, and an application to Australian environmental disaster data illustrates the model's ability to capture zero-inflation and dependence in real-world scenarios.

Russ Tedrake discusses transitioning from discrete Markov chain analysis to temporal difference (TD) learning using function approximation to handle continuous state spaces. He provides a crash course on least squares function approximation, comparing neural networks to linear function approximators. He notes that linear approximators, which use a linear combination of non-linear basis functions (such as radial basis functions, polynomials, or Fourier decompositions), allow for explicit analytical solutions.

Tedrake demonstrates that robot manipulator dynamics are linear in their parameters, making system identification a linear least squares task. He then extends TD learning to function approximation by using eligibility traces on the parameter vector $\alpha$ rather than on discrete states. Finally, he introduces Least Squares Temporal Difference (LSTD) learning, an efficient batch method that uses all experienced data to solve for the steady-state parameter vector, avoiding the need for a learning rate or initial guess.

This work studies profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade through online learning, aiming to design an algorithm that minimizes regret relative to the best mechanism in hindsight. Conversely, they prove that in the adversarial setting, no learning algorithm can achieve sublinear regret with respect to a $2/3 + \epsilon$ fraction of the optimal profit. Additionally, the authors apply their findings to the joint ads problem, improving the regret bound from $O(T^{3/4})$ to $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$.

Mediation analysis identifies the mechanisms through which interventions affect outcomes. While structural equation modeling (SEM) is the standard for identifying latent mediators, it relies on the often unachievable assumption of no unmeasured confounding. To address this, researchers have used rank-preserving models (RPMs) that allow for omitted covariates under a no-effect-modifier assumption. The authors introduce the Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model (RAPSEM), a novel framework that integrates RPM with latent variable modeling to enable robust mediation analysis despite measurement error and omitted confounders.

This study investigates whether transformers can learn to infer transitive relations by evaluating their ability to solve the graph connectivity task using connectivity information provided as individual training examples. Experimental results indicate that transformers excel at learning connectivity in low-dimensional grid graphs, where they can utilize a low-dimensional vertex-embedding heuristic, but struggle with disconnected chain graphs. While scaling model size facilitates learning for grid graphs, it does not significantly improve performance for disconnected chain graphs. Conversely, scaling the graph size improves performance for disconnected chain graphs by increasing the number of nodes per chain. For higher-dimensional grid graphs and disconnected chain graphs with many components, increasing the number of nodes (data scaling) is more effective than increasing model size.

The United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment to Reisdorf Brothers, Incorporated on the plaintiffs' Clean Water Act and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act claims. The court found the plaintiffs failed to present triable issues of fact regarding continuous or intermittent pollutant discharges or regulatory violations. Additionally, the court upheld the dismissal of the plaintiffs' state law adverse possession claim due to the district court's proper exercise of discretion in declining supplemental jurisdiction and affirmed the denial of the defendant's request for attorney fees.

Using data from the PREVEND study, researchers employed multi-state modelling to examine the relationship between KDIGO kidney disease risk stages and new-onset heart failure (HF). The study found that forward transition rates between risk stages increase exponentially with age and are higher in men than in women. While the relative risk of developing HF associated with advanced KDIGO stages attenuates with age, the absolute risk increases. The findings suggest that slowing kidney disease progression in middle-aged populations may reduce the incidence of new-onset HF.

This study aimed to develop a valid and reliable scale to measure prospective teachers' attitudes toward values education through distance education. The resulting 36-item scale demonstrated high reliability, with Cronbach Alpha coefficients of .97 and .96 for the respective factors. The study concluded that the scale provides a valid tool for identifying attitudes, though results may be limited by the specific participant demographic and university setting.

Parental obesity increases a child's risk of obesity through biological mechanisms in eggs and sperm. Obese fathers may transmit non-coding RNAs in sperm that influence offspring fatness, while obese mothers may pass on defective mitochondria or altered nutritional building blocks in eggs that affect embryonic metabolism. Research suggests that lifestyle interventions like diet and exercise can improve egg and sperm quality, potentially reducing obesity susceptibility in offspring.

This study introduces "surveillance pedagogy" to examine the relationship between slavery, pedagogy, and digital surveillance. Using Michel Foucault’s theory of panopticism, the author argues that surveillance serves as a tool for extraction and control in both historical slavery and contemporary "surveillance capitalism." The text highlights how the extraction and "textualization" of human experience—once used in plantation settings to monitor enslaved people—is mirrored in modern digitalization, where algorithms and platforms like Google mine student data to condition behavior and generate profit. Ultimately, the author posits that the historical legacies of slavery and the master/slave binary are inextricably linked to modern pedagogical practices and the commercialization of learning.
